business_summary.text: J.G. Chemicals is India's largest manufacturer of zinc oxide, producing it largely from recycled zinc scrap at plants in West Bengal and Naidupeta, Andhra Pradesh, for tyre, ceramics, pharma and other industries.

call_points.text: Dahej's ₹100 Cr capex from internal accruals is expected to earn about ₹900 Cr of sales at full capacity.
call_points.versus_prior: new: no earlier sales potential in memory

call_points.text: Dahej civil works are in advanced stages and equipment installation has commenced; the project is moving as per plan.
Dahej is targeted to lift non-rubber revenue contribution from 15% to 30% over the next few years.
FY26 saw record volumes across major vehicle categories, with PV at 46.43 lakh units, an all-time high.
Tyre industry capex plans have been upgraded to ₹20,000–25,000 crore over the next three years, materially higher than a few quarters ago.
Higher energy, logistics and procurement costs were passed on to all customers from 1 April 2026.
Raw material requirements remain fully secured despite war-led disruption to global zinc dross flows, and supply to every customer was uninterrupted.
JGC now offers over 90 specialised grades of zinc oxide, up from 80+ at end of FY24.
Recycled rubber project pilot trials drew positive customer feedback; a commercial-scale project is being worked on, with capex and timeline to be shared later.
Naidupeta solar Phase 1 is live, with further ESG initiatives under evaluation.

operating_notes.text: Q4FY26 consolidated revenue ₹286.17 Cr, up 27.6% YoY; cost of materials and goods was 83.7% of revenue against 81.7% a year earlier.
FY26 cash from operations ₹43.58 Cr against capex of ₹39.03 Cr; borrowings ₹6.45 Cr at 31 March 2026.
The company recognised a net loss of ₹15.01 million as 'Loss of inventories due to fire' under Other Expenses, with an insurance claim lodged.
FY26 revenue segmentation: Rubber & Tyre 85.0%, Pharma & Chemicals 8.2%, Agri 3.7%, Others 3.1%.
Dahej greenfield: 11.43 acres, over 40,000 MTPA, ₹100 Cr investment, 100% internal accruals, potential revenue ₹900 Cr.
JGC offers over 90 specialised grades of zinc oxide, up from 80+ at end of FY24.
Of the ₹165 Cr IPO gross proceeds, ₹131.466 Cr was utilised by 31-Mar-2026, leaving ₹33.534 Cr parked in fixed deposits and the monitoring account.
R&D centre capex of ₹6.058 Cr had only ₹1.796 Cr spent by Q4FY26; ICRA noted purchases did not align with prospectus vendor specifications.
Of the ₹165 Cr IPO gross proceeds, ₹131.466 Cr was utilised by 31-Mar-2026, leaving ₹33.534 Cr unutilized and parked in fixed deposits and monitoring accounts.

timeline.summary: Anirudh Jhunjhunwala HUF, as promoter, declares holding 40,000 J.G. Chemicals shares on 31-Mar-2026 with no encumbrances during FY2025-26.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹286.17 Cr, net profit to shareholders ₹18.21 Cr.
J.G. Chemicals' FY26 earnings presentation (14 May 2026) reported FY26 revenue ₹973 Cr, up 14.7%, and said the ₹100 Cr Dahej greenfield plant would start commissioning in H1FY27.
ICRA's final monitoring agency report for Q4FY26 showed ₹131.466 Cr of J.G. Chemicals' ₹165 Cr IPO gross proceeds utilised, with ₹33.534 Cr unspent and the R&D centre spend behind schedule.
On May 14, 2026, J.G. Chemicals reported its Q4 FY26 monitoring agency report showing ₹131.47 Cr utilized out of ₹165 Cr IPO proceeds.
J.G. Chemicals submitted the audio recording of its Q4 and FY26 earnings call on May 16, 2026.
Jayanti Commercial Private Limited, as promoter of J.G. Chemicals Limited, declared on June 1, 2026, holding 31,83,900 shares with no encumbrances during FY2025-26.
